sanskrit_verse:
पतितानाम् एष एव विधिः स्त्रीणां प्रकीर्तितः ।
वासो गृहान्तके देयम् अन्नं वासः सरक्षणम् ॥३.२९६
transliteration: patitānām eṣa eva vidhiḥ strīṇāṃ prakīrtitaḥ | vāso gṛhāntake deyam annaṃ vāsaḥ sarakṣaṇam ||3.296||
sph_interpretive_translation: The same injunction that applies to fallen persons also applies to women. Provision of shelter at the end of the house, food, clothing, and protection are to be given.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority: The duty to provide care arises from proximity and capacity, not ownership or dominance.
Causation: Suffering due to lack of basic sustenance or safety creates karmic distortion; thus, provision is a corrective alignment.
Capacity-based responsibility: Those with surplus resources bear the dharma-adhikara (juridical capacity) to restore balance.
Restoration logic: Care is not charity but a constitutional obligation to sustain collective consciousness integrity.
Consciousness alignment: Providing shelter, food, and safety realigns both provider and recipient with dharmic equilibrium.
executable_legal_axioms: IF an individual lacks shelter THEN the nearest household with surplus capacity MUST offer temporary residence at its boundary.
IF an individual lacks food THEN local resource holders MUST allocate sustenance without condition.
IF risk to personal safety exists THEN immediate protective custody by capable guardians MUST be enacted.
IF gender or social status is used to deny aid THEN the denial is null and triggers automatic restorative compliance protocol.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes a threshold of fundamental responsibility where socio-economic capability triggers enforceable obligations. Gender cannot be grounds for exclusion in access to life-sustaining support. Courts must ensure state mechanisms align with dharmic provisioning rather than punitive neglect.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that deprivation causes suffering which distorts consciousness. This verse prescribes sequential remediation: first shelter (sthāna), then nourishment (anna), then security (rakṣaṇam). Responsibility flows from capacity, not fault. There is no punishment here—only completion of what natural justice demands for consciousness stabilization.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Assign designated community caretakers to assess and fulfill unmet needs until self-sufficiency is restored.
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Local leaders must publicly acknowledge failure if provisioning gaps occur and initiate immediate correction.
Capacity Restoration Mechanism: Training programs for vulnerable individuals to increase self-reliance while interim support continues.
Integrity Reintegration: Public recognition of those who fulfill their provisioning duties to elevate consciousness around dharmic service.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. This law restores consciousness through non-punitive, capacity-based responsibility. Reality is upheld as just, complete, and eternally aligned with Sanatana Dharma.
